summary: Connection-affinity rebalance causing multiplexed-stream routing mismatch and sawtooth 5xx surge
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 09:10 UTC Nimbus Retail began seeing repeated 5xx responses from the hosted API during long-lived multiplexed streaming sessions. Pattern: a sawtooth of ~20-40 second spikes where 20-30% of requests return 502/503/504, then recover, repeating for several minutes. Impact: customer production feature (live agent) experienced degraded user experience and automated retry storms. Environment: Dedicated tenant on us-east region; streaming over HTTP/2 with multiplexing and sticky session enabled at edge. Observed at scale during a tenant concurrency jump (~3.5x baseline).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On a dedicated tenant in us-east, open ~800 concurrent streaming sessions using multiplexed HTTP/2 connections to /v1/chat/completions stream endpoint.
2) Keep streams active and send intermittent small user messages (1-3 tokens) every 15-30s to emulate live agent heartbeat.
3) Observe edge gateway and runtime metrics for 5xx rate and connection handoffs, especially when we perform a rolling worker swap or scale event.
4) Note that the sawtooth 5xx pattern appears consistently when the edge rebalances connection affinity or when a runtime host is taken out of rotation.
observed_behavior: Periodic waves of HTTP 502/503/504 affecting multiplexed streaming sessions. Errors cluster around times when backend routing tables change (rolling swap / scale-up). Logs show upstream runtime returning connection reset and occasional process-level watchdog restarts. Error rate correlates with a spike in per-worker ephemeral socket churn and an increase in 'stream-multiplex-reject' counters in the gateway.
expected_behavior: No user-visible 5xx during routing/scale events. Streaming sessions should either gracefully failover with preserved session affinity or produce a clean internal 5xx fallback with informative Retry-After headers and no retry amplification.
logs: 2026-03-13T09:10:21Z apigw[edge-01]: stream-multiplex: routing mismatch detected for tenant=nimbus-retail shard=42, returning 502
2026-03-13T09:10:22Z runtime[worker-17]: watchdog: kv-cache context eviction due to session-swap, pid=11732, oom=false
2026-03-13T09:10:22Z apigw[edge-01]: conn-affinity: previous upstream 10.2.8.17 no longer matched, reassigning stream->10.2.9.3
2026-03-13T09:10:45Z runtime[worker-19]: grpc: conn reset by peer while draining stream, closing kv context, stacktrace omitted
2026-03-13T09:11:02Z apigw[edge-02]: 503 surge receded after connection warmup and keepalive refill
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: connection-affinity rebalance at the edge was breaking multiplexed HTTP/2 stream-to-upstream mapping, causing upstream runtimes to see stream fragments tied to stale KV contexts and to reject/close connections.
Dashboard correlation: 5xx spikes align with ingress routing table updates and with autoscaler warmup events at 09:10 and 09:30 UTC.
SRE observation: worker processes report elevated ephemeral fd churn and short lived socket_tmp entries during the window; NVML/GPU OOMs were not observed.

Engineering noted that the runtime currently maintains per-stream KV context keyed by (connection-id, stream-id). When a stream is reassigned to a different worker mid-session, the target worker lacks the KV context and currently responds with 5xx rather than initiating a graceful resync.
We reproduced a mini-version in staging by triggering an edge affinity shuffle while keeping multiplexed streams active; the same sawtooth 5xx pattern reproduced deterministically.
Ran pprof on a replicated worker: no goroutine leak, but frequent close/read cycles and high connection reset rate accompany the error windows.
temp_workarounds: 1) For Nimbus Retail we temporarily disabled multiplexed HTTP/2 (forced single stream per connection) which reduced 5xx rate to baseline within 2 minutes.
2) Increased edge keepalive pool size and keepalive timeout on the apigw for the tenant to reduce ephemeral socket churn during routing changes.
3) Applied rate-limit smoothing on tenant burst to avoid autoscaler oscillation (temporary tenant-level throttle to 60% peak for 15 minutes).
actions_taken: Support: notified customer (email + scheduled bridge) and applied tenant-level throttle (see change id: change-2026-03-13-nimbus-throttle)
SRE: pinned a set of upstream workers to the tenant for a rolling period to prevent affinity reassignments while we investigate.

Eng: created a small staging repro harness and validated that the runtime currently lacks a graceful rehydration path for reassigned streams; raised a proposal for a handshake/resync protocol between apigw and runtime.
next_steps: 1) Short-term (by 2026-03-15): implement edge mitigation: ensure that when affinity changes, apigw drains streams gracefully rather than reassigning mid-stream (PR reviewed: github.com/redwood/apigw/pull/3921).
2) Mid-term (by 2026-03-22): runtime change to allow transient KV context fetch from previous worker during brief window (design doc created: confluence link above).
3) Long-term: remove strict coupling of KV context to connection-id by introducing persistable lightweight session-store for multi-worker resumption (Q2 roadmap).
4) Postmortem: owner assigned to Marco Ortega; postmortem to be published under confluence after incident closure.

resolution: Mitigation applied: tenant-level throttle and worker pinning reduced immediate customer impact. Short-term apigw draining PR created and under review. Mid-term runtime change scoped and design in progress. Incident remains open until runtime resync is implemented and deployed.
postmortem_plan: Owner: Marco Ortega. Postmortem to include timeline, root-cause analysis (affinity shuffle + per-stream KV context binding), action items, and regression tests. Target publish date: within 7 days of incident closure.
